question: From a point P outside a circle, two tangents PA and PB are drawn. If the length of PA is 7 units, what is the length of PB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The lengths of **tangents** drawn from an **external point** to a circle are always **equal**.

Given that **PA** and **PB** are two tangents from the same point **P**.

∴ PA = PB

Since PA = 7 units, then PB = 7 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of tangent PA = 7 units

External point = P

**Formula Used:**

For any circle, the lengths of two **tangents** drawn from an external point to the circle are equal (Theorem of tangents).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1603d26ca9f283ee9345d8d7a4ceca6d22b275439ee7c0ce7e4170cb55e0795.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the center of the circle be **O**.

⇒ **OA** and **OB** are radii of the circle perpendicular to tangents **PA** and **PB** respectively.

⇒ In right-angled triangles **ΔOAP** and **ΔOBP**:

⇒ OA = OB (Radii of the same circle)

⇒ OP = OP (Common hypotenuse)

⇒ ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90°

⇒ By **RHS congruence criterion**, ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP.

⇒ By **CPCT** (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles), PA = PB.

⇒ Since PA = 7 units, PB = 7 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (OA ⊥ PA).

Power of a Point

For an external point P, the square of the tangent length is equal to the product of the secant segments: PA² = PB² = PT × PS.

Angle Bisector Property

The line segment joining the center of the circle to the external point P bisects the angle between the two tangents (∠APO = ∠BPO).</p
